topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture's learning objectives and the conceptual framework of the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Growth Signal Autonomy and Proliferation Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how mutations in cell surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades drive sustained proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how cancers arrest terminal differentiation and maintain proliferative precursor states in both hematopoietic lineages and the intestinal epithelium.

topics.label: Evasion of Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how mutations in p53 and the balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins prevent programmed cell death in cancer cells.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells achieve indefinite division by maintaining telomeres and escaping p53-mediated senescence checkpoints.

topics.label: Altered Energy Metabolism and Oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells rewire metabolic pathways toward aerobic glycolysis and generate oncometabolites that alter gene regulation.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the necessity, early onset, and regulatory balance of activators and inhibitors governing blood vessel formation in tumors.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Diagnostics of Cancer Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the multi-step metastatic cascade, diagnostic tracking via lymph node biopsies and circulating tumor cells, and the genomic features of disseminated tumors.

topics.label: Summary and Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reflecting on the collective nature of cancer hallmarks and recent conceptual frameworks.
